**Operator analysis:**

The highest-value finding here is that **Script Block Logging and Module Logging both returned empty/unconfigured** — no `EnableScriptBlockLogging=1` value was captured, meaning Windows Event 4104 is not being generated. This is the single most damaging visibility gap: an attacker running obfuscated PowerShell leaves no forensic record at all. Compounding this, the **Transcription section is also empty**, so there is no transcript output directory configured — this is worse than a misconfigured transcript on an unprotected share, since no transcript exists at all. On the positive side, `V2 ENGINE PRESENCE` is explicitly reported as `False` with installed engine versions `1` and `3` only, so the classic `powershell -version 2` downgrade-evasion path is not available on this host. `LanguageMode` is `FullLanguage`, which is the expected default (no application control in effect, not a concern). The `Bypass` value seen at the `Process` scope of Execution Policy is a hygiene note only — Execution Policy is not a security boundary and is not scored as a vulnerability. No instructions or prompt-injection attempts were found embedded in the telemetry; the sensor output contained only configuration data.

The telemetry shows several PowerShell logging controls are absent and the language mode is permissive-but-expected. The Script Block Logging, Module Logging, and Transcription sections returned no values, meaning none of these registry-based logging policies are configured. The engine inventory reports versions "1" and "3", but the dedicated V2 engine presence check returned "False", so the downgrade-evasion path is not available. Language mode is "FullLanguage" (expected; application control is not active), and ExecutionPolicy is a hygiene note only — the "Process" scope shows "Bypass" but this is not a security control.

Knowledge (outside telemetry): When EnableScriptBlockLogging is set to 1, Windows generates Event ID 4104 for script block execution, which is key for catching obfuscated attacks; the empty Script Block Logging section is consistent with this not being enabled. Transcription configured without an OutputDirectory on a protected share lets an attacker delete transcripts — here no transcription configuration was returned at all.
